semantics.summary: Returns the factorial n!; the addendum explicitly defines 0! as 1.

printed-pages: Chapter 13, printed pp. 13-33–13-34 (same feature: combined update scan pp. 14-1–14-2)
notes: The 3.5 addendum page images were checked. The source describes an integer-expression argument and explicitly defines 0! = 1.

The companion German book explicitly places FACT among the 3.5 additions and says the function is defined only for integer values; it reports calculation through n=421 (printed pp. 477–478). Its FACT(421) example is printed in scientific notation, so the exact numeric representation and overflow boundary remain unresolved.
The existing prototype evaluates only a restricted literal subset; it has no stable registry handler mapping and is not a complete implementation.

A typed Rust runtime handler is registered. Checked u32 inputs, u128 results, and Rust errors for invalid domain or overflow are implementation-boundary choices, not original-interpreter conformance claims.

support.pending-reason: Original numeric range/representation and reference-interpreter overflow/error behavior remain unverified.
